title.narrative: Skills Strengthening for Industrial Value Enhancement Operation

description.narrative: The objective of the Skills Strengthening for Industrial Value Enhancement Operation Project for India is to improve access to quality and market-driven vocational training provided in ITIs and apprenticeships. India's gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 7.6 percent in 2015-16 steadily recovering from a low of 5.1 percent in 2012–13. This GDP growth was largely supported by robust consumption growth on the expenditure side and strong growth in the services sector, averaging more than 9 percent between 2012 and 2015, on the production side, although a recovery of industrial value added in 2015–16 was notable. With growth, poverty has declined rapidly from 38.9 percent in 2004–05 to 21.6 percent in 2011–12 (1.90 purchasing power parity per day) at a pace significantly faster than that witnessed in earlier periods. Poverty reduction was supported by greater rural-urban integration, increase in nonfarm wage employment, especially in construction, and higher rural wage growth. Given the cooling of the latter two trends in the past three years, it is likely the pace of poverty reduction moderated. Going forward, India's growth prospects remain bright. A million youth will enter the labor market every month for the next two decades, and India will soon have one of the youngest and largest working-age populations in the world. These demographic dynamics and a rising age-savings profile are likely to generate significant volumes of savings and investment over the coming years. The average schooling of the working-age population, and, consequently, worker productivity, will increase by at least a full year until 2030 even with no further improvements in the educational attainment of today's youth (that is, simply because younger cohorts are better educated) and could rise much faster if further progress is achieved on the education agenda. The proportion of population living in urban areas is expected to rise to 40 percent in 2030 from around 30 percent today, reinforcing productivity-boosting agglomeration effects. Combined, these effects are likely to form the foundations of India's strong growth for decades to come.
To improve access to quality and market-driven vocational training provided in ITIs and apprenticeships

condition.narrative: GoI to carry out a gender study on terms and conditions agreed with the Association to determine the demand and supply sideconstraints for women to undertake skills training and/or be part of apprenticeship initiatives, and thereafter transition into thelabor market.

GoI to ensure that the participating States: (a) invite ITIs to submit Institute Strategic Plans (ISPs) for financing through PBGrant Agreements in accordance with the Operations Manual; (b) screen the ISP proposals in accordance with the protocols andeligibility criteria set forth in the Operations Manual; and (c) enter into tri-partite written agreements (with MSDE and theawardee ITI) for the provision of the performance based grant under terms and conditions set forth in the Operations Manual and theFinancing Agreement.
GoI to implement the agreed Program Action Plan
GoI to invite all States to enter into MoUs with GoI for the provision of performance-based funding terms and conditions set forthin the Operations Manual and the Financing Agreement.

GoI to prepare, approve and implement an Operations Manual, and thereafter carry out the Operation, and cause the participatingStates, the ITIs/Institute Management Committees (IMCs), and Industry Clusters (ICs) to carry out their respective activities underthe Operation, in accordance therewith.
GoI to undertake the verification process to certify the fulfillment of the DLIs in accordance with terms of reference agreed withthe Association.

GoI to: (a) through the participating States, invite ICs to submit IAI proposals for financing through IAI Grants in accordancewith the Operations Manual; (b) screen the IAI proposal in accordance with the protocols and eligibility criteria set forth in theOperations Manual; and (c) enter into tri-partite written agreements (with the respective participating state and the awardee IC)for the provision of the IAI Grant under terms and conditions set forth in the Operations Manual and the Financing Agreement.

GoI to: (i) carry out the Project (IPF component), or cause it to be carried out, in accordance with the Tribal Peoples PolicyFramework and each additional assessment or plan required to be prepared and implemented thereunder; and (ii) ensure that the it isbenefiting from the Operation maintain functional environment and social management systems guaranteeing Industrial TrainingInstitute's (ITI) compliance with the GoI's relevant environmental and social regulations prevalent at the time, including thoserelated to safe work environment for staff and students alike.

Government of India (GoI) to maintain a national program implementation unit (NPIU) within the Directorate General of Training(DGT) for the carrying out of the day-to-day implementation of the Operation

MSDE to select and engage the services of a program management consulting firm (PMC) in order to assist the NPIU and the StateProgram Implementation Units (SPIUs) with the Operations planning and implementation.

Participating States to establish and maintain SPIUs within the respective line Department responsible for the long-term training,to serve the state-level focal unit for the carrying out of the day-to-day implementation of the Operation's activities within therespective State.

title.narrative: IR Indicator 6.1: Number of ICs receiving IAI Grants that have reached a female enrollment of 12% in their respective apprenticeship programs

comment.narrative: The end-of-project target has already been achieved. As of May 2024, female enrolment across 12 industry clusters had exceeded 20 percent of trainees enrolled.

title.narrative: IR Indicator 1.1: Percentage increase in enrollment across ITIs with signed PB Grant Agreement

comment.narrative: The increase in enrollment compared to the baseline has reached 13.39 percent (in 2022-23), displaying a significant increase over the past two enrollment cycles. During the 2020-21 academic year enrollments had decreased due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Enrollment rates recovered in 2021-22 academic year, reaching 10 percent. Enrollment rates further recovered in 2022-23 academic year, reaching 13.39 percent.

title.narrative: IR Indicator 4.1: Number of Participating States that have conducted tracer studies

comment.narrative: A total of 15 states (excluding pilot for Haryana) have completed their tracer study. Out of this 14 state tracers studies have been verified by the Independent Verification Agency (IVA) and the verification of 1 state is currently under process by the IVA. Further, 5 more states have completed the Tracer study and the report are currently awaiting approval from the State Steering committee

title.narrative: Number of Participating States that have reduced the vacancies of sanctioned trainers posts by at least 20% in government ITIs

comment.narrative: The end-of-Project (EOP) target was achieved in September 2021. Since that time two additional states have reduced the vacancies of sanctioned trainer posts by 20 percent. Further, 5 States are reported to have maintained zero vacancy levels consistently.

title.narrative: Number of ICs that have introduced at least 2 different apprenticeship programs within their participating (member) industries

comment.narrative: 30 ICs have commenced training in two trades as per the STRIVE norms. Verification has also been completed for 21 ICs by the Independent Verification Agency. Data collection and internal verification is ongoing for the remaining ICs.

title.narrative: Increase in the number of graduates from ITIs that have signed PB Grant Agreements

comment.narrative: The results for the 2022-23 cohort is 39.2 percent over the baseline. During academic year 2021-22 supplementary and trainees who had failed from 2014 to 2020 batches were provided an opportunity to appear/re-appear for the exam leading to an increase in numbers. Further, the marks uploaded and results processing for some of the trainees were recently updated resulting in an increase in the number of graduates. Note: Enrollments in the trades of 2 year duration are conducted every alternate year leading to reduced number of enrollments and subsequently graduates only each alternate year.

title.narrative: IR Indicator 5.1: Number of CTS trades for which ICT-based teaching and learning packages have been developed

comment.narrative: The development of 5 trades has been completed and has been approved by DGT and verified by the Independent Verification Agency (IVA).

title.narrative: IR Indicator 5.2: Number of CITS trades upgraded

comment.narrative: The development of 5 trades has been completed and has been approved by DGT and verified by the Independent Verification Agency (IVA).
The end-of-Project target of 400,000 beneficiaries was achieved by April 2022. The number of direct beneficiaries has reached 624,025 (134,165 females) as in May 2024.

title.narrative: IR Indicator 4.2: Percentage of trainees in government ITIs who are from ST populations

comment.narrative: Per policy and legislation, ITIs are required to reserve a quota for Scheduled Tribes (STs) and Scheduled Castes (SCs). Per the updated enrollment data the end-of-project target is overachieved at 9.30 percent in 2020-21. By Mid-Term Review in February 2021, the percentage of STs in government ITIs had reached 7.8 percent, thereby exceeding the end-of-Project (EOP) target of 4 percent. For the academic year 2022-23 the ST enrollment stood at 7.96 percent The disaggregated data target is being maintained and the 4 percent end-of-project target is being consistently surpassed.

title.narrative: IR Indicator 1.2: Percentage of trainees undergoing OJT across ITIs with signed PB Grant Agreements

comment.narrative: The current analysis of the 2021-22 cohort indicates an overachievement of the end-of-project target of 25, reaching to 44.14 verified percent. The data has been by the Independent Verification Agency (IVA).

title.narrative: Number of teachers who have completed pre-employment or in-service distance learning/blended modules

comment.narrative: By September 15, 2021 the total number of teachers who had received training was 20,000. The end-Project (EOP) target is 20,000. This target was achieved in August 2022. As of February 2024, 27,500 teachers/instructors have received training. Additionally 115 instructors, DGT and State officials were trained in Project Management and leadership training in 4 batches at IIM Kozhikode.

title.narrative: Percentage of graduates from ITIs that have signed PB Grant Agreements who are in gainful employment one year after graduation

comment.narrative: The tracer study to ascertain the gainful employment of graduates has been completed, reviewed and comments provided by the World Bank team. The final report, after incorporating the inputs shared by WB a long with comments received from NPIU, has been submitted by the vendor. As per the final report, overall placement rate was 49. Including apprentices in the calculation/analysis, placements are up to 52.2 percent

title.narrative: Female enrollment rate in ITIs with signed PB Grant Agreements

comment.narrative: Following the closing of admissions/enrollment for 2022-23, the current female enrolment rate in project ITIs is reported to be 19.50 percent. The end-of-project Year 7 (2023-24) target of 15 percent has been overachieved (19.5 percent), verified, claimed and disbursed in February 2024.
